headline: Memory makers say HBM is sold out through next year; Gemini enterprise pricing moves

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's ten to eleven UTC on Friday, October thirtieth. This is Aradio.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The memory makers' filings this morning say high-bandwidth memory is allocated through next year. Alphabet and the other buyers have locked in supply, and everyone else is paying more for ordinary DRAM.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Google also cut list prices for its enterprise Gemini tier. In its launch video, a product lead framed it as a response to usage growth, not to competition.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Rivals have not matched yet. Give it two weeks before reading too much into that. Price cuts like this usually take a quarter to show up in anyone's numbers.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Start with memory, because it touches everything else on the board. The filings describe allocation, not just high prices: buyers without long-term contracts are being told to wait.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: And the knock-on effect is in ordinary DRAM. As fabs move capacity to the high-bandwidth parts, contract prices for the memory in laptops and phones keep rising.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: We have moved the memory story up a notch, to developing with an importance of four. The next data point is the memory makers' own guidance later this week.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: On Gemini, the price cut is aimed at seats, not tokens. Businesses that already pay for Workspace get more of the assistant bundled in.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: If Microsoft answers on Copilot pricing, this becomes a price war. If it does not, it is Google buying adoption.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: What to watch: memory guidance this week, and any move on enterprise assistant pricing from Microsoft or OpenAI.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's Aradio. We'll be back when the picture changes.
